title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No mathematical error is visible. Several symbols are ambiguous in the scan: whether the crossed Ẑ in the expression for M̃_{ρ,σ} is kept, and the exact meaning of 𝔖^{+∧} and M^∧ (defined elsewhere, §49 VI and (150)). The identifications are only up to the semidirect-product actions defined on earlier pages, so they cannot be fully checked from this page alone.

ideas.what: Profinite limit over the Fermat tower of level-N symmetry group schemes, taking compatible sections (Δ), giving groups of the form Ẑ*⋉(…)
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of the profinite Fermat tower / Ẑ-points of the limit of Fermat curve symmetry groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications, Annals 1986); Anderson; Coleman
ideas.where_published: Possibly touched on in La Longue Marche (1981), unsure

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the arithmetic fundamental group (moduli of type (1,1) over Q, and from π_1(Q)) into the Fermat-tower symmetry group, whose abelian part is the cyclotomic character
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on the Fermat tower (Ihara power series, Jacobi sums, Anderson's hyperadelic gamma function)
ideas.where_published: Spirit of Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche (Galois action on towers); not explicitly for the Fermat tower to my knowledge

ideas.what: Decomposition into three components; the N_ρ component reduces to the cyclotomic condition, while surjectivity of the G_{ρ,σ}, G^{⇆} and N_σ ≃ Ẑ*⋉Ẑ components is posed as an open question
ideas.modern_name: Image / surjectivity of Galois and GT-type representations on the abelianized-tower quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara school (image of Galois in the Fermat-tower automorphisms)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets up the action of the arithmetic fundamental group (of a (1,1) moduli-type object, and of π_1(Q)) on the profinite tower of Fermat curves. He does so in terms of explicit profinite group schemes Ẑ*⋉(Ẑ×𝔖^{+∧}), as a refinement of the cyclotomic character. This anticipates by several years Ihara's 1985–86 study of Galois action on the Fermat tower.
missed.quote: L'homomorphisme 𝓜 → M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)^, relatif à la tour des courbes de Fermat
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for the Ihara/Anderson/Coleman theory of Galois action on Fermat curves. The notes also include the moduli fundamental group (not just Gal(Q̄/Q)), a GT-flavoured variant.

missed.claim: Surjectivity of 𝓜 → G_{ρ,σ}=Ẑ*·𝔖^{+∧}, of M^! → G^{⇆}=Ẑ*·M^∧, and of π_Q^{ét} → N_σ=Ẑ*⋉Ẑ is posed but not settled (continued on the next page).
missed.quote: on est amené à se demander si ces deux homs sont surjectifs
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Comparing these questions with the known computations of the Galois image on the Fermat tower (Ihara's power series, Anderson) could show whether they are answered. The variant with the moduli fundamental group may not be addressed.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets up a Galois/fundamental-group action on the profinite Fermat tower, a theme later developed by Ihara and others without reference to these notes. However, the content is set-up and notation; the substantive questions only appear on the next page, and the specific groups are not interpretable without earlier sections.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'relative à la tour des courbes de Fermat' (not 'relatif[?] à').
The marginal note reads roughly: 'Le Δ indique qu'on prend [les] sections qui satisfont [aux] conditions de compatibilité', referring to (215).
In the N_ρ line, read 'O_{12}^*(Ẑ)^' (subscript 12), not 'O^*_Ω'.

After (216): 'où les opérations de Ẑ* sur le groupe facteur à droite sont explicitées dans les sections précédentes. On notera que, moyennant des ajustages de notations et de définitions, les groupes profinis Z_{ρ,σ} etc. précédents seraient construits ... directement, en termes de (𝔖^{+∧}, 𝔖^{⇆∧}=M^∧), dans §49 VI.'
Final line likely reads 'qui comme d'habitude se décompose en' (continuing 'trois' on the next page), not 'qui commutent d'habitude se décomposer en'.
In the M̃_{ρ,σ} line, the factor is Ẑ×𝔖^{+∧}; the Ẑ appears partly overwritten but is probably kept.
